description: The browser wgpu shell's folder door (ticket 26/09/30 NON-DESTRUCTIVE-HISTORY-EDITING, S2-W2C): the browser build has no filesystem, so — like React's worker — it keeps a folder- or file-bound document's archive through the dev host's backbone route (`GET|PUT /semio-backbone?uri=&documentId=&schema=`, the Vite `semioBackboneVitePlugin`), asked through the page-owned `semioWgpuHostIo` door because the shell runs in the frame Worker. `requests` are what the Rust shell sends (`json`, compared as JSON values) and the one fetch the page makes for each (`fetch`); `answers` are what the page hands back for each HTTP outcome (`page`) and what the shell reads from them: a read's archive bytes (base64, `null` = nothing written yet), a write's acknowledgement, or the refusal it tells.

requests.name: writing a folder document carries its schema and its archive bytes

answers.name: a stored archive is read as its bytes
a document nothing has written yet reads as no archive
a host without the route refuses the read by its status
a fetch that never reached the host is told as itself
a write the host failed is refused by its status
